prompted_for: Standards we design to (original of concept-m-standards; became StandardsGrid: numbered standard cards joined by thin lines)
art_direction: desktop and mobile side by side
composition: oversized two-line headline top-left, grid below
3 x 4 grid of equal outlined cards filling the sheet
dot-grid texture block top-right as negative space
mobile column at right with the same cards stacked and a fade-out at the bottom
sheet framed by zone letters (A1, A2, B1, B2) in the margins
layout_devices: thin routed connector lines with arrowheads running between cards like a circuit or pipe route
breadcrumb header line 'section 04 / ...' over a ruler tick bar
drawing-sheet zone references in the margin
vertical tick ruler beside the mobile stack
'scroll for more' steel-blue bar on mobile
palette: warm limestone off-white headline and card titles
muted steel-blue grey for mono codes, connectors and margin labels
pale steel-blue tinted bottom bar on mobile
typography: heavy bold grotesk all-caps headline, tight leading
tiny mono meta labels (view width, version number)
rendering: no shading or gradients except the mobile fade
line_and_texture: 1 px off-white card outlines with square corners
hairline steel-blue connector lines with small arrowheads
dashed vertical breakpoint divider between desktop and mobile
motion_implied: connector lines draw from card to card in order 01-12
cards light up in sequence as the route reaches them
ruler ticks scroll with page progress
t2i_keywords: outlined rectangular cards with square corners
thin routed connector lines between cards
desktop and mobile view side by side
high contrast type on dark ground
t2i_prompt: Flat desktop UI mockup with a matching mobile view beside it, no device frame, no people. Deep navy background, sheet framed like an engineering drawing with zone letters in the margins and a ruler tick bar under a small monospace breadcrumb. Oversized bold all-caps off-white headline top-left, a patch of fine dot grid to its right. Below, a precise grid of square-cornered outlined cards, each with a monospace number and code line and a bold caps title for <CONTENT>. Thin steel-blue routed connector lines with small arrowheads run between cards like a circuit. Mobile view stacks the cards beside a tick ruler and fades into a steel-blue scroll bar.
signature_idea: A dozen standards laid out as a numbered card grid wired together by one thin routed line, like a circuit on a drawing sheet.
strengths: names each standard with its code: instantly scannable for QA and validation leads
numbered index gives order and a sense of completeness
drawing-sheet frame reads as engineering, not marketing
mobile translation is clear and plausible
weaknesses: connector lines carry no meaning, routing is decorative and busy
uniform 12-card grid is close to a generic card wall
heavy bold caps headline is off the brand's light headline weight
dense and dark; little air between cards
brand_fit_why: Navy, limestone and steel-blue line work, square corners and mono codes fit, but the heavy bold caps type and crowded grid miss the light Geist headlines and space-as-material calm.
